caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular piece of woven textile with a repeating geometric pattern composed of blue and off-white threads. The main pattern consists of large, blue ovals outlined by smaller white and blue blocks, arranged in a regular grid. Inside each oval, there are smaller, intricate geometric details including horizontal and vertical lines forming crosses and rectangles, contributing to a symmetrical and balanced appearance. Between the ovals, blue and white squares and rectangles alternate, reinforcing the grid structure. At the bottom of the textile, there are two horizontal bands containing smaller geometric blue and white patterns, separated by strips with off-white zigzag designs. The fabric extends slightly below the lower bands, revealing a fringe of off-white threads. The drawing is set against a plain, light beige background, and some text is visible in the lower left corner.
title: Woven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
